{{recipe}}

This recipe is a translation of a recipe in ''Ma cuisine 2 500 recettes'' by August Escoffier, written in French and published in 1934 (''Purée de Marrons'', page 522). The recipe has been reformatted in line with modern recipe writing conventions.

==Ingredients==
*Whole [[Cookbook:Chestnut|chestnuts]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 pinch [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], if needed
*[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (950 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) chicken, veal, or beef [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]

==Procedure==
# Carefully split the skin at the thin (protruding) side of the chestnuts, and place them on a baking tray that contains a little water.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] chestnuts in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for around 7–8 minutes. This will make it easier to peel them.
# Peel the chestnuts.
# Cook the chestnuts in just enough [[Cookbook:Consommé|consommé]] for them to be damp. The chestnuts should not be hard but not be too well cooked either.
# Pass the cooked chestnuts through a fine [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]].
# Put the puree into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], then add a pinch of sugar and a pinch of salt if necessary.
# Add fine butter and turn off the heat once thick.
